outcome: propensity to seek medical attention from a professional
cohort: Antenatal women aged 15-36 years (mean 27.4 years), predominantly multiparous and in their second or third trimester of pregnancy, attending an antenatal clinic in an urban metropolis in Nigeria.
finding: Tokophobia was prevalent among antenatal women in this study, with 11.5% experiencing intense fear of childbirth, and over a quarter (38.2%) expressed a desire to seek professional care.
mod_finding: No statistically significant association was found between previous mode of delivery and tokophobia prevalence.
cross-section timing: During the antenatal period, specifically when women were in their second or third trimester of pregnancy.
